title: p0055
universal_lens: A coach's 25-year empirical search reveals falling on loose balls yields negative expected yardage except in end zones. Time perception dilates recovery window (τ_perceived ≫ τ_actual), causing suboptimal commitment. Optimal policy: replace fall-recovery with scoop-advance, maximizing E[Δy] under opponent pressure.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian updater: prior P(advantage|fall) ~ Beta(α,β) from 25-season record; likelihood of observed near-turnover updates posterior to near-zero. Conformal prediction set for recovery-yardage excludes fall-action with 1-α coverage. Decision threshold: scoop if P(advance > 0 | state) > 0.5 + ε.
gse_mapping: State-transition: loose-ball state S ∈ {fall, scoop, opponent}. Transition kernel T(S'|S,a) favors scoop→advance with probability p_scoop > p_fall. Value iteration V(S) = max_a Σ T(S'|S,a)[R(S,a,S') + γV(S')] yields policy π*(S)=scoop. Breakdown when τ_actual < neuromuscular latency.

primitives.name: Perceptual Time Dilation in Loose-Ball Recovery
primitives.verbatim_quote: I distinctly remember that as I lay on the ball it seemed like a full minute at least before anybody dropped on me.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: τ_perceived: subjective duration [s]; τ_actual: objective duration [s]; κ: dilation factor [dimensionless]
primitives.assumptions: Stress-induced time dilation follows scalar multiplication; κ constant across similar high-stakes recoveries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: κ → 1 when arousal low; κ undefined if τ_actual < 0.1 s (sensorimotor floor).

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state-observation latency: agent's internal clock runs faster than game clock, causing delayed commitment. Telemetry: eye-tracking + inertial measurement unit (IMU) timestamps at ball contact.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of subjective-to-objective recovery time measured via post-play interview vs video analysis.

primitives.name: Expected Yardage Differential: Fall vs Scoop
primitives.verbatim_quote: 30 WINNING FOOTBALL picked up that ball more easily than I fell on it and I could certainly have made those twentyfive yards and perhaps a touchdown without any further doubt.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y_scoop: yards gained on scoop-advance [yd]; Y_fall: yards gained on fall-recovery [yd]; ΔY: expected yardage differential [yd]
primitives.assumptions: Opponent pickup probability p_opp > 0.5 when ball carrier falls; scoop-advance success probability p_scoop > 0.7; turnover cost = -E[field position loss].
primitives.breakdown_regime: ΔY ≤ 0 inside own 5-yard line (safety risk) or when τ_actual < 0.5 s (no scoop time).

layer2.mapping: GSI reward model: R(s,a) = ΔY. GSE transition: scoop action shifts state to 'controlled advance' with probability p_scoop. Telemetry: play-by-play tracking of loose-ball outcomes (n ≥ 500).
layer2.telemetry: Empirical ΔY from game film: mean yards gained on scoop vs fall recoveries.

primitives.name: Empirical Policy Update from 25-Season Evidence
primitives.verbatim_quote: years of pretty close contact with the game and a fairly wide study of its records,
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: π_t: policy at season t [dimensionless]; a ∈ {fall, scoop}; s: game state; endzone: s where goal-line recovery nullifies advance need.
primitives.assumptions: Stationary opponent behavior; 25-season sample sufficient for policy convergence; endzone exception is absorbing state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Policy reverts if opponent adapts (p_opp|scoop increases) or rule changes alter loose-ball dynamics.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Bayesian policy optimization with conjugate prior. GSE: deterministic policy switch at t=25. Telemetry: season-over-season loose-ball recovery success rate.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of fall-recovery attempts per game pre/post policy change.

primitives.name: Endzone Exception: Zero-Advance Recovery
primitives.verbatim_quote: ball, except when this occurred behind the opposing goal-line where, of course, there was no need
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: 1_{s∈endzone}: indicator [dimensionless]; Y_fall, Y_scoop: yards [yd]; both zero in endzone.
primitives.assumptions: Touchdown awarded immediately on possession in endzone; no fumble risk after control established.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rule change allowing fumble in endzone; or if scoop enables lateral for extra point.

layer2.mapping: GSI: likelihood truncation at boundary. GSE: absorbing state with reward R=6 (TD). Telemetry: endzone loose-ball recovery outcomes (n ≈ 50).
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of endzone recoveries via fall vs scoop; turnover rate in endzone.

reasoning_traces.think:
The coach's narrative encodes a sequential decision problem under perceptual distortion. Primitive 1 quantifies τ_perceived = κ·τ_actual with κ≈20-30 (minute vs 2-3s). This dilation causes overcommitment to fall-recovery: the agent believes they have time to secure possession, but opponent scoops in τ_actual. Primitive 2 computes ΔY = E[Y_scoop] - E[Y_fall] ≈ 25 yd - (-turnover) > 0. The 25-yard figure is a lower bound on scoop-advance expectation; fall-recovery expectation is negative due to opponent pickup probability p_opp > 0.5. Primitive 3 formalizes the policy update: after N=25 seasons, posterior P(advantage|fall) ≈ 0, so π*(fall)=0 for non-endzone states. This is a Bayesian update with Beta(α,β) prior where α≈few, β≈many. Primitive 4 handles the boundary condition: in endzone, both actions yield Y=0 (touchdown), so fall is acceptable. Duality: time dilation (κ) and yardage differential (ΔY) are coupled via τ_actual — if τ_actual < neuromuscular latency (~0.2s), scoop becomes infeasible, forcing fall. Failure mode: opponent adapts by attacking scoop attempts (increasing p_opp|scoop), shifting ΔY ≤ 0. Leakage veto: κ must be estimated per-player, not assumed constant; ΔY must be recomputed per field position.

Coach's policy switch to scoop forces opponent to defend larger state-space (scoop left/right/advance), increasing their cognitive load. Opponent's best response: assign dedicated 'scoop defender' reducing p_scoop, potentially restoring fall viability — a Stackelberg equilibrium shift.
